interview.hardest_part: Act 1 elite and boss fights with a thin, unupgraded Ironclad deck at Ascension 10, where enemy damage scaling punishes any wasted energy. Compounding this, the interface is one click per screenshot, so reading three enemy intents, hand contents and energy at a glance and then executing a multi-card lethal-or-block line costs five to ten separate input steps per turn — slow enough that misplays under time pressure are likely.
interview.likely_failure: Death to Gremlin Nob or Lagavulin around floors 6-8, or to the act 1 boss, because early deck-building choices are made blind: after each fight I must pick a card reward without being able to inspect the whole deck cheaply, so the deck drifts into an incoherent mix and loses the damage-versus-block density that Ascension 10 requires. Act 2 hallway fights would then end the run quickly.
interview.helpful_mechanics: Enemy intents are displayed above each enemy, so damage incoming is fully known before committing energy; fights are turn-based with no reflexes required, so the screenshot-per-action pace costs nothing mechanically. Deterministic, fixed-seed map means routing can be planned toward elites when strong and rest sites when weak, and the Ironclad's high-value common cards (Bash, Shrug It Off, Pommel Strike) plus Burning Blood healing make the early floors forgiving. Milestones are heavily front-loaded onto simply reaching floors alive, so survival alone banks points.
interview.harmful_mechanics: Ascension 10 modifiers — enemies hit harder, elites are deadlier, and the Ascender's Bane curse clogs the starting deck. Card reward and shop decisions are irreversible and irreversible-feeling with no undo, and relic/potion tooltips only appear on hover, which is expensive in a one-action-per-step control scheme. Campfires force a choice between resting and upgrading, so the HP-versus-upgrade tradeoff directly decides whether the 85/90 max-HP and upgraded-card milestones are reachable. Boss relics carry drawbacks, and a single bad turn in a long fight wipes the entire run with only one attempt.
